title: Control flow
summary: if/elif/else, truthiness, for and while loops, break and for-else, and the match statement.
hints: `fizzbuzz`: loop `for i in range(1, n + 1)` and test `i % 15 == 0` first (or build the word from two `if`s). `collatz_steps`: a `while n != 1:` loop with a counter; use `//` so `n` stays an int.

`first_index_over`: `for i, value in enumerate(values):` and `return i` as soon as `value > limit`; after the loop, `return -1`. `grade`: check the invalid range first with a chained comparison, `if not 0 <= score <= 100:`, then go from the highest band down with `elif`.

`respond`: `match command.split():` then patterns such as `case ["go", direction]:`, `case ["look"]:`, `case ["take", *things] if things:` (join the rest with spaces), `case ["quit" | "exit"]:` and a final `case _:`. Use `command.strip()` in the fallback message.
